description: A library system where books, members, and copies are nodes; a member borrows a copy through a loan edge carrying due-date and renewal-count, and a walker traces which members are currently overdue by following borrower edges out from each book.

A company org chart where employees are nodes connected by reports-to edges; a walker starting at any employee climbs the chain to the CEO, or descends to list every person in a manager's reporting tree at any depth.

A delivery network where warehouses and drop-off points are nodes joined by road-segment edges carrying distance and traffic-delay; a walker finds the cheapest multi-hop route for a package from origin to destination.

A social app where users are nodes connected by follows edges and posts are nodes attached to their author; a walker builds a user's home feed by visiting everyone they follow and collecting posts within the last day.

A university catalog where courses are nodes linked by prerequisite edges; a walker checks whether a student can enroll in a target course by verifying every prerequisite chain back to courses already completed.

A manufacturing inventory where parts are nodes and assemblies reference their sub-parts through composed-of edges carrying quantity; a walker explodes a top-level product into its full multi-level parts list.

A messaging app where conversations are nodes holding participant edges to users and message nodes chained by replies-to edges; a walker reconstructs a threaded conversation by following reply chains from any message back to the root.

A single-elimination tournament where matches are nodes linked by advances-to edges to the next round's match; a walker starting from the championship match traces backward to reconstruct the full path any given player took to reach the final.

A cooking app where recipes are nodes connected to ingredient nodes via requires edges, and ingredients are linked to each other by substitutable-for edges; a walker suggests a modified recipe by swapping unavailable ingredients for their nearest substitute.

An academic paper database where papers are nodes joined by cites edges; a walker computes a paper's influence by counting how many hops away other papers are that eventually cite it, stopping at a configurable depth.

A genealogy app where people are nodes connected by parent-of and married-to edges; a walker computes the relationship between any two people (cousin, aunt, grandparent) by finding the shortest path through parent edges.

A city traffic simulator where intersections are nodes and streets are directed edges carrying current congestion; a walker reroutes a driver in real time whenever an edge's congestion crosses a threshold.

A package manager where libraries are nodes and depends-on edges carry version constraints; a walker performs a topological traversal to compute a valid install order, flagging any circular dependency it detects.

A wiki-style knowledge base where articles are nodes connected by links-to edges; a walker suggests related reading by doing a bounded-depth traversal from the article the reader is currently viewing.

A SaaS billing system where accounts are nodes linked to plan nodes via subscribed-to edges and usage-event nodes attach to accounts via logged edges; a walker aggregates usage across an account's billing period to compute the invoice.

An open-world game where map zones are nodes joined by passage edges gated by required items; a walker checks whether a player carrying a given inventory can reach a target zone from their current location.

A staffing platform where employees are nodes with has-skill edges to skill nodes, and projects are nodes with requires-skill edges; a walker finds every employee whose skill set fully covers a project's requirements.

A city utility network where houses are nodes fed by transformer nodes through supplies edges, and transformers connect upstream to substations; a walker traces which houses lose power when a given transformer or substation fails.

An events app where events are nodes, users are nodes linked by invited and attending edges, and events reference each other via follow-up-to edges for recurring series; a walker builds a user's schedule by visiting every event they're attending and flagging time conflicts.

A version-control visualizer where commits are nodes linked by parent-of edges (with merge commits having two parents); a walker finds the common ancestor of two branch-tip commits by walking backward from each until the paths converge.

A public-health contact-tracing tool where people are nodes and contact-with edges carry a timestamp and duration; a walker starting from an infected person traces every person reachable within a given number of contact-hops and time window.

A property registry where parcels are nodes and owned-by edges link them to owner nodes, with owner nodes able to be companies that are themselves owned-by other owner nodes; a walker resolves the ultimate beneficial owner of any parcel by following ownership chains.

A music platform where tracks are nodes, artists are nodes linked by performed-on and produced edges, and tracks reference sampled-from edges to earlier tracks; a walker computes every artist who contributed, directly or through a sample chain, to a given track.

A warehouse robotics system where shelf locations are nodes joined by aisle-adjacent edges carrying travel time; a walker plans the shortest visiting order for a robot that must pick items from a scattered set of shelf nodes before returning to the dock.

An enterprise access-control system where roles are nodes linked by inherits-from edges and permissions attach to roles via grants edges; a walker resolves the full effective permission set for a user by climbing their role's inheritance chain.

A restaurant reservation system where tables are nodes joined by adjacent-to edges for tables that can be merged, and reservations are nodes assigned to tables via seated-at edges; a walker finds a combination of adjacent tables that can be merged to fit a large party.

A support ticketing system where tickets are nodes linked by escalated-to edges to other tickets or agent nodes, and agents connect to team nodes; a walker finds the current owner of a ticket by following the escalation chain to its most recent link.

A food-safety traceability system where batches are nodes linked by derived-from edges tracing raw ingredients through processing steps to a final product; a walker traces every upstream batch that fed into a contaminated final product for a recall.

An airline booking system where airports are nodes and scheduled-flight edges carry departure/arrival times and airline; a walker searches for a valid multi-leg itinerary between two airports where each connecting flight departs after the previous one lands.

A codebase analysis tool where source files are nodes linked by imports edges; a walker detects circular import chains and computes the full transitive set of files affected by a change to any given file.

A fraud-detection system where claims are nodes linked to person and vehicle nodes via involved-in edges; a walker flags suspicious clusters by finding groups of claims that share the same person or vehicle node across multiple incidents.

A mentorship platform where members are nodes connected by mentors edges (which can chain, since a mentor can also have their own mentor); a walker builds a member's full mentorship lineage and separately lists everyone they influence downstream.

A theme park app where rides and pathways are nodes joined by walkable-to edges carrying current walk time, and rides carry live wait-time; a walker recommends the lowest total-time route to ride a wishlist of attractions in some order.

A legal research tool where court cases are nodes linked by cites-as-precedent edges; a walker checks whether a given ruling has been effectively overturned by tracing forward through cases that cite it as overruling.

A smart-home network where devices are nodes joined by paired-with edges representing mesh connectivity, and automation-rule nodes link to trigger and action devices; a walker determines which devices become unreachable if a given hub device goes offline.

A finance app where funds are nodes linked by holds edges to company nodes (with weight), and companies can themselves be holding companies with holds edges to subsidiaries; a walker computes a fund's total indirect exposure to a given company through nested holdings.

A hospital system where patients are nodes linked to doctor nodes via referred-by edges that can chain across specialists; a walker reconstructs the full referral path that led a patient to their current specialist appointment.

A trading game where players are nodes linked by proposed-trade edges carrying offered and requested resources; a walker searches for a cycle of trades among three or more players that leaves everyone better off than a direct two-player trade would.

A news aggregator where articles are nodes linked by covers-same-event edges when they report on the same underlying story, and articles cite sources via sourced-from edges; a walker clusters same-event articles and traces the earliest original source in each cluster.

A research administration tool where researchers are nodes linked by co-authored-with edges (weighted by paper count) and grouped into lab nodes; a walker finds the shortest collaboration path between two researchers who have never directly co-authored a paper.
